events.title: Hamlin Halloween Haunt
events.desc: Speaking of quintessential fall activities, this community haunt will have you singing songs around the campfire, taking a hayride and playing Halloween-themed games. Wear your costumes for the photo booth!

events.title: ‘Trolls: A Field Study’ at Northwest Trek and Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium
events.cost: Included with admission ($17–$32; ages 2 and younger are free) or membership
events.loc: Northwest Trek and Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium
events.desc: It’s opening weekend for “Trolls: A Field Study,” and it’s the perfect weekend for a zoo day. Meet eight trolls at Northwest Trek and four at Point Defiance Zoo (and tell them I said hi!). The whimsy, creativity and thoughtful details of each troll will wow the whole family. There are even more reasons to visit both zoos this weekend: Hoot ‘n’ Howl is on Friday and Saturday at Northwest Trek an…

events.title: Fracture!
events.cost: Pay-what-you-want admission, starting at $10 per person
events.loc: Pacific Science Center , 200 Sue Bird Court N., Seattle
events.desc: As if math wasn’t scary enough on its own! This experience has elements of an escape room, a haunted house and live theater, all rolled into one. Solve problems and save the day. (Come 1–4 p.m. for the family-friendly version, or 7–10 p.m. for after-dark scares.)

events.title: Diwali Family Festival at SAAM
events.cost: Free; reserve tickets for timed activities
events.loc: Seattle Asian Art Museum , 1400 E. Prospect St., Seattle
events.desc: Celebrate Diwali at this fantastic cultural festival. The Seattle Asian Art Museum will have a youth art exhibition, live performances and special activities throughout the day. Make art with artist Deepti Agrawal, get a custom henna design and indulge in flavorful dishes from the Spice Waala food truck.

events.title: AutumnFest Family Fun at Evergreen Arboretum and Gardens
events.loc: Evergreen Arboretum & Gardens , 145 Alverson Blvd., Everett
events.desc: The votes are in! Three honorary pet mayors will be inaugurated this weekend at the arboretum: a dog mayor, a cat mayor and a stuffie mayor. Celebrate the occasion, meet puppies from the Everett Animal Shelter and make sure you’re registered to vote in the real election. Plus, kids can help plant spring-flowering bulbs (and even take some home).

events.title: Zap: A Day of Electric Discovery
events.loc: Karshner Museum and Center for Culture & Arts , 309 Fourth St. N.E., Puyallup
events.desc: I love hands-on activities, and this free event is jam-packed with them. Build your own electrical circuit, learn about wind turbines and renewable energy, and encourage a love of science. (And let someone else answer your kids’ endless questions about how things work for a change.)

events.title: Issaquah Goes Apples
events.loc: Historic Shell Station and Downtown Issaquah , 232 Front St. N., Issaquah
events.desc: This is the place to be if you haven’t had fresh-pressed apple cider yet this fall (it’s on my bucket list!). Play apple-themed games, build a scarecrow and snap photos as you go. Plan to shop the markets, with both farm and artisan goods.

events.title: Indigenous Peoples’ Day at the Burke Museum
events.loc: Burke Museum , 4303 Memorial Way N.E., Seattle
events.desc: The Burke Museum is an incredible museum to visit anytime, but this is a special opportunity to go for free! In celebration of Indigenous Peoples’ Day, enjoy a special performance from the WestShore Canoe Family. Then see artist Siobhan Amelia at work in the Artist Studio and explore the museum’s exhibits.

events.title: Benaroya Hall Open House
events.desc: Check out the newly renovated Benaroya Hall with a full day of free festivities. Musicians, storytellers and more artists take to the stage. The day ends with a free performance from the Seattle Symphony Orchestra and The Head and the Heart (but you’ll have to get there early to snag tickets for that!).

events.title: Pumpkin Painting Social
events.loc: Copperworks Distilling , 7324 N.E. 175th St., Suite A, Kenmore
events.desc: Having watched our carved pumpkins disintegrate on our front steps over the last two weeks, I am thinking painted pumpkins are the way to go. This fun annual bash includes free pumpkins for little ones, with plenty of paint pens and craft supplies to bring their pumpkin to life. If cookies are more your speed, there will be sugar cookie decorating too. Costumes encouraged!
